subtitle: How a Dispossessed Prince and a New Army Drove Ava Back to the Chindwin

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a battlefield ridge by a great river
panels.action: Raja Gambhir Singh stands on a grassy rise above a wide river that twists away like steel, planting a tall Manipuri standard into the earth as distant Burmese forces retreat toward forested hills.

dialogue.text: In the smoke of the First Anglo–Burmese War, Gambhir Singh, an exiled prince with a new paid army, drives Ava to the Chindwin and wins back Manipur by treaty.

i18n.hi: पहले एंग्लो–बर्मी युद्ध के धुएँ में, निर्वासित राजकुमार गम्भीर सिंह अपनी तनख़्वाहदार सेना से आवा को चिंदविन तक भगाते हैं और मणिपुर संधि से वापस लेते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a weathered face in exile
panels.action: A younger Raja Gambhir Singh, lean and intense, sits in a dim shelter in Sylhet, a rolled map of Manipur spread before him as rain lashes a thatched roof beyond.

dialogue.text: When Burmese armies overran Manipur, Gambhir Singh fled west. The Cheitharol Kumbaba remembers a prince in exile, staring at maps and counting every loss.

i18n.hi: जब बर्मी फ़ौजों ने मणिपुर रौंदा, गम्भीर सिंह पश्चिम भागे। ‘चैथारोल कुम्बाबा’ में वही राजकुमार है, बनवास में नक्शे तके हुए, हर हार गिनता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a colonial bungalow, contrasting uniforms and robes
panels.action: In a modest Company bungalow in Sylhet, Gambhir Singh in Manipuri attire faces a seated British officer in frock coat and epaulettes; between them on a table lies a map marked ‘Assam’, ‘Cachar’ and ‘Ava’.

dialogue.text: To the British in Bengal, Ava threatened Assam and Sylhet. To Gambhir Singh, Ava held his homeland. Their needs met in one dim room, over a map of the eastern hills.

i18n.hi: बंगाल के अंग्रेज़ों के लिए आवा असम और सिलहट पर मंडराता ख़तरा था। गम्भीर सिंह के लिए, आवा ने उनका वतन पकड़ा था। दोनों की ज़रूरतें एक मद्धिम कमरे में, पहाड़ी नक्शे पर मिलीं।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of a small training ground
panels.action: On a clearing edge in Cachar, Gambhir Singh strides past ranks of Meitei recruits drilling with muskets under the eye of a British sergeant, jungle rising behind them like a wall.

dialogue.text: Here was the innovation: not unpaid lallup labour, called out for war and then sent back to fields, but a small, paid levy—five hundred men at first—armed and drilled with Company muskets.

i18n.hi: यहीं नयी चाल चली गयी: अब बेगार वाला लालुप नहीं, जो खेत छोड़कर युद्ध को निकले; अब छोटी, तनख़्वाहदार टुकड़ी—शुरू में बस पाँच सौ—कम्पनी की बंदूकों से लैस, क़ायदे से drilled।

panels.shot: wide shot of camp life at dusk
panels.action: At dusk in the levy camp, Gambhir Singh sits with veteran officers under a lantern, counting coins into small bags as soldiers queue; beyond, tents and stacked muskets line a muddy field.

dialogue.text: Pay meant men could serve full-time. It meant drilling in volleys, marching in files, a small standing force ready when orders came. It was a new way of making war in Manipur.

i18n.hi: मज़दूरी ने सिपाहियों को पूरा वक़्त दिया। अब वे पंक्तियों में चल सकते थे, दाग़ सकते थे, एक छोटी स्थायी फ़ौज, हुक्म मिलते ही तैयार। मणिपुर में जंग का यह नया ढंग था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the levy on the move through hills
panels.action: A column of Gambhir Singh’s levy winds along a narrow ridge path above clouds, their bayonets glinting, as he rides near the front, pointing toward the unseen Manipur valley ahead.

dialogue.text: In 1825, as the First Anglo–Burmese War spread, the levy moved east. British officers had their own columns. But in the valley, it was Gambhir Singh’s name that crossed lips and courtyards.

i18n.hi: १८२५ में, जब पहला एंग्लो–बर्मी युद्ध फैला, यह टुकड़ी पूरब बढ़ी। अंग्रेज़ अफ़सर अपनी–अपनी टुकड़ियों के साथ चले। पर घाटी में, आँगन से चौपाल तक, नाम गूंजा गम्भीर सिंह का ही।

panels.shot: sweeping wide of Imphal valley with approaching troops
panels.action: The Imphal valley opens under a grey sky as Gambhir Singh’s force descends a pass; scattered Manipuri villagers watch from fields and bamboo groves as the column advances toward the old capital.

dialogue.text: The Cheitharol Kumbaba notes each step as he re-entered the valley. Villages saw not fleeing refugees but a disciplined line with muskets at the shoulder, moving to reclaim their capital.

i18n.hi: ‘चैथारोल कुम्बाबा’ उसके घाटी में लौटते हर क़दम को दर्ज करता है। गाँवों ने अब भागते शरणार्थी नहीं देखे, बल्कि कंधे पर बंदूकें टिकाए अनुशासित पंक्ति देखी, जो राजधानी वापस लेने चली थी।

panels.shot: medium shot before the old palace gate
panels.action: Facing the weathered gate of Kangla, Gambhir Singh stands with his officers; behind him, levy soldiers take positions as smoke from cooking fires curls above the palace compound.

dialogue.text: Burmese garrisons had brought their own rule. Now, faced with an armed, organized return, they fell back. There was fighting, there was flight, and then the old palace saw a Meitei prince again.

i18n.hi: बर्मी चौकियों ने अपनी अलग हुकूमत लाई थी। अब, इस हथियारबंद, संगठित वापसी को देखकर, वे पीछे हटे। कहीं जंग हुई, कहीं भगदड़; फिर पुराने महल ने दोबारा एक मैतेइ राजकुमार देखा।

panels.action: In the inner court of Kangla, Gambhir Singh stands in ritual attire as priests and nobles watch; behind them, levy soldiers rest their muskets on the ground, bridging courtly tradition and new military power.

dialogue.text: In the royal chronicle, his return is marked with rituals and offerings. Yet outside the sacred space, the real guarantee of that return stood on parade—his levy, still on British pay.

i18n.hi: राज–इतिहास में उसकी वापसी पूजा–यज्ञों से दर्ज है। पर पवित्र चौहद्दी के बाहर, उस लौटने की असली गारंटी सलामी में खड़ी थी—उसकी वही टुकड़ी, अब भी कम्पनी के वेतन पर।

panels.shot: tense medium shot in a war tent with joint command
panels.action: In a canvas war tent lit by candlelight, Gambhir Singh leans over a rough map with a British officer; their fingers trace a line eastward through Tamu toward the Chindwin as aides watch in silence.

dialogue.text: In British records, Company columns lead and allies follow. In Meitei memory, Gambhir Singh plans and advances. The maps show the same path: Manipur to Tamu, then to the Chindwin.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ कागज़ों में कम्पनी की टुकड़ियाँ आगे, दोस्त फ़ौजें पीछे दिखती हैं। मैतेइ याद में, गम्भीर सिंह ही योजना बना कर बढ़ते हैं। नक्शे पर राह एक ही है: मणिपुर से तामू, फिर चिंदविन तक।

panels.shot: dynamic battleline wide along forest edge
panels.action: At the edge of dense forest near Tamu, Gambhir Singh’s levy forms a firing line, smoke curling from their muskets, as distant Burmese formations regroup near palm trees and earthen works.

dialogue.text: The levy pushed beyond the valley. At Tamu, British artillery and Meitei musketeers moved together. Ava’s frontier posts felt the pressure of this combined force from the hills.

i18n.hi: टुकड़ी घाटी से आगे निकल गयी। तामू में, अंग्रेज़ तोपें और मैतेइ बंदूकची साथ–साथ चले। आवा की सरहदी चौकियों ने पहाड़ियों से उतरती इस मिली–जुली ताक़त का दबाव महसूस किया।

panels.shot: long shot of march beside a great river
panels.action: The column advances along a sandy bank of the Chindwin River, its broad waters glinting under harsh sun as Gambhir Singh rides at the edge, watching Burmese positions vanish into the distance.

dialogue.text: Step by step, they drove Ava’s forces back to the Chindwin. For the British, this was one front among many. For Manipur, it was the line beyond which Burmese claims would be pushed.

i18n.hi: कदम–कदम पर वे आवा की फ़ौजों को चिंदविन तक ठेलते गये। अंग्रेज़ों के लिए यह कई मोर्चों में से बस एक था। मणिपुर के लिए, यह वही लकीर थी जिसके आगे बर्मी दावे धकेले जाने थे।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Gambhir Singh planting a flag by the river
panels.action: On a small rise by the Chindwin, Gambhir Singh presses a Manipuri standard into the earth, his face set and calm; behind him soldiers rest, some gazing across the water toward Ava’s side.

dialogue.speaker: raja_gambhir_singh
dialogue.text: Beyond this river, they shall not claim our valley again.

i18n.hi: इस दरिया के पार, वे हमारी घाटी पर दोबारा दावा नहीं करेंगे।

panels.shot: close-up of the Treaty of Yandaboo being signed
panels.action: Inside a Burmese pavilion at Yandaboo, a British plenipotentiary and a representative of Ava sit opposite each other, quills poised above a parchment as attendants look on respectfully.

dialogue.text: On 24 February 1826, at Yandaboo, Ava’s envoys signed. In that treaty text, they renounced all claims over Manipur, Assam and other eastern territories to the Company.

i18n.hi: २४ फ़रवरी १८२६ को, यानदबू में, आवा के दूतों ने दस्तख़त किये। उस संधि में उन्होंने कम्पनी के हक़ में मणिपुर, असम और दूसरे पूरबी इलाक़ों पर अपने सारे दावे छोड़ दिये।

panels.shot: insert close-up of the treaty parchment
panels.action: A tight view shows elegant script on the treaty parchment, certain lines underlined, while a hand folds the document, sealing it with wax bearing the Company’s emblem.

dialogue.text: C.U. Aitchison’s later collection would preserve the words. For Manipur, this paper mattered: it fixed in writing what the Chindwin retreat had already forced on the ground.

i18n.hi: सी. यू. ऐटचिसन की बाद की संकलन ने उन शब्दों को बचा रखा। मणिपुर के लिए यह काग़ज़ ज़रूरी था: इसने लिखाई में वही बाँध दिया जो चिंदविन से पीछे हटने ने ज़मीन पर मनवा लिया था।

panels.shot: reflective medium shot of Gambhir Singh receiving news
panels.action: In Kangla’s audience hall, Gambhir Singh listens as a messenger kneels, offering a folded document; British officers stand aside, while Meitei nobles watch, their faces a mix of relief and calculation.

dialogue.text: The treaty was not signed in his hand. Yet its lines reflected his campaigns. British cannons and Meitei muskets together had made Ava’s promise to leave Manipur binding.

i18n.hi: संधि पर दस्तख़त उसके हाथ से नहीं हुए। फिर भी हर पंक्ति में उसके अभियान झलकते हैं। अंग्रेज़ तोपें और मैतेइ बंदूकें मिलकर ही आवा का मणिपुर छोड़ने का वादा पक्का करा पायीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of rebuilding in Imphal valley
panels.action: Under a clear sky, Gambhir Singh walks through a busy Imphal street as carpenters raise new houses, farmers lead cattle, and levy soldiers stand guard near a half-built storehouse.

dialogue.text: War’s end did not restore the old world. With the levy still on pay, markets opened under guard. Fields were sown again. A small kingdom now stood between Ava and the Company.

i18n.hi: जंग ख़त्म होने से पुरानी दुनिया वापस नहीं आयी। टुकड़ी अब भी तनख़्वाह पर थी, बाज़ार पहरे में खुलने लगे। खेतों में फिर बोआई हुई। आवा और कम्पनी के बीच अब एक छोटा, पर खड़ा हुआ राज था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Gambhir Singh in council with British and Meitei officials
panels.action: In a council chamber, Gambhir Singh sits at the head of a low table, flanked by Meitei ministers; across from them, a British political agent listens, notes in hand, as they discuss a map.

dialogue.text: British reports stressed their protection. Meitei chronicles stressed his rule. Between these two records lay a reality: an independent Manipur, its throne held up by an alliance and a standing levy.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ रपटें अपनी हिफ़ाज़त का दम भरती रहीं। मैतेइ इतिहास उसकी हुकूमत पर ज़ोर देता है। इन दो रिकॉर्डों के बीच एक सच्चाई थी: एक आज़ाद मणिपुर, जिसका तख़्त गठजोड़ और स्थायी टुकड़ी ने संभाल रखा था।

panels.shot: contemplative close-up of Gambhir Singh looking toward the eastern hills
panels.action: At dusk on a fort wall, Gambhir Singh rests his hand on the haft of the standard he once planted, gazing toward the distant eastern hills as the levy’s campfires glow below.

dialogue.text: Gambhir Singh’s story on the eastern frontier is one of exile, alliance and a paid army that pushed Ava to the Chindwin—reminding us that liberation can hinge on new institutions as much as courage.

i18n.hi: पूरब की सरहद पर गम्भीर सिंह की दास्तान बनवास, दोस्ती और तनख़्वाहदार सेना की है, जिसने आवा को चिंदविन तक धकेला—याद दिलाती है कि मुक्ति सिर्फ़ दिलेरी से नहीं, नये इदारों पर भी टिकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Dispossessed Prince and a New Army Drove Ava Back to the Chindwin
